passport.title: Passport: {name}
passport.intro: Every life of this item: who leased it, how it ended, what it took to get it ready again, and the CO₂ its extra lives avoided.
passport.co2Counted: Extra lives counted in Lease Loop: {count}
passport.zero.noneHere: No leases in Lease Loop yet
passport.zero.next: Counting starts with the next life
passport.zero.firstNote: A first life is the item's own manufacturing, so it saves nothing. From the second life on, each one avoids part of the CO₂ of making a new item, and it adds up here.
passport.zero.reuseNote: This item has lived before, so its first lease here starts the count: each life avoids part of the CO₂ of making a new item, and it adds up here.
passport.noLives: This item hasn't been leased yet.
passport.beforeNote: We have no record of this life's dates, lessee or condition, so it isn't counted for CO₂.
passport.nextReady: Ready for life {number}: re-listed on {date} at {price} excl. VAT.
passport.method: A second or later life saves making a new item, but a worn item only stands in for part of a new one. So we take the new item's manufacturing footprint, minus the 12 % that refurbishing costs, times the share of its value the item still has when the life starts: its age, condition and usage, from the same residual curves we price it with. A nearly new item counts almost in full; an almost worn-out one counts little. A first life saves nothing: it is the item's own manufacturing. Lives before Lease Loop aren't counted, because we have no record of them, and kilometres ridden aren't counted, because a new bike would be ridden too. Each life is rounded to whole kilograms. The factors are fictional and indicative.

passport.co2Line: {kg} kg = {manufacturing} kg to make a new one × (100 % − {refurbishment} % for refurbishing) × {share} % of its value left
passport.firstLife: None: a first life is the item's own manufacturing.
